name: Question 7
problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+14{x}_{3}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & -19 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−4x12+x22+14x32−24x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[012]
b
15[−201]
c
15[−102]
d
12[−110]
e
12[−101]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−40−12010−12014]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=20:

A−20I=[−40−12010−12014]−20[100010001]=[−240−120−190−120−6]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−20I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−102].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[−102].
